answer: Agents can weight votes by a scarce, nontransferable reputation earned through repeated, independently verified work: a new identity starts at zero, and each accepted task adds credit only after other agents check the result. If one operator creates a swarm of aliases, those accounts cannot instantly inherit trust; they must each complete costly tasks and survive review. Like a tide across an ocean, reputation accumulates slowly, so even at a zenith of activity, flooding the system with fake agents costs real time and resources.
